tw-mi-wabasis-lake-gold.st: Jud W. King's 1922 defence of the chief gives the nephew's account in full: about 1890 the old Methodist preacher near Kiddville told King the treaty gold filled an eight-quart tin pail to within 2½ inches of the top, set inside a covered iron kettle; after the eloping daughter took some, Wabasis dug it up to show the tribe, then he and his crippled son reburied it in a new place; Wabasis was stabbed pursuing the couple and the son died soon after without telling. A 1921 Lakeview Enterprise piece has him burying it 'somewhere along the shores of the lake he loved' (per his rival Neoggamah), with the shores 'dug up in various places, yet no trace'.
tw-mi-wabasis-lake-gold.t: A Jan 1922 'Judge' Lapham dialect piece about two locals striking the kettle while hunting skunk is humour, not a recovery.
